statement: (i) Solve $2^{x}=5$ exactly and give the approximate value. (ii) Solve $\ln(x+1)+\ln(x-1)=\ln 3$. (iii) Show that $e^{x}=x^{2}$ has exactly one real root and that it is negative.
solution: (i) $x=\frac{\ln 5}{\ln 2}=\log_{2}5\approx 2.3219$. (ii) $\ln((x+1)(x-1))=\ln 3\Rightarrow x^{2}-1=3\Rightarrow x^{2}=4$, and $x>1$ is required, so $x=2$. (iii) Let $h(x)=e^{x}-x^{2}$. For $x>0$, $h'(x)=e^{x}-2x$ has minimum at $x=\ln 2$ with value $2-2\ln 2>0$, so $h$ is increasing on $[0,\infty)$ with $h(0)=1>0$; thus no positive root. For $x<0$, $h'(x)=e^{x}-2x>0$ (both terms positive), so $h$ increases from $-\infty$ (as $x\to-\infty$) to $h(0)=1$, crossing zero exactly once. Hence exactly one real root, and it is negative.
hints: Take logs for the first equation.
Study h(x)=e^x - x^2 on each sign of x.
